title: Iran, Qatari mediators hold third day of talks to end US-Iran war
gist: Iranian negotiators held a third day of talks with Qatari mediators in Doha on a deal to end the eight-month US-Israeli war on Iran, including a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days of an agreement with Washington. Trump pledged no new attacks before the Nov. 3 midterms but has not ruled out strikes afterward, while Iran threatens to hit US and Israeli targets in neighboring countries.

themes.theme: Strait of Hormuz and oil supply

insights.claim: Iranian and Qatari negotiators developed a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days of a potential agreement with Washington, according to Iranian FM Abbas Araqchi.
insights.speaker: Abbas Araqchi
insights.so_what: A Hormuz reopening would be a major bearish catalyst for oil prices and tanker risk premia.
insights.locator: Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera quoted Araqchi

insights.claim: The eight-month-old US-Israeli war on Iran continues to disrupt global oil supplies and spill over across the Middle East.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Ongoing supply disruption keeps an elevated geopolitical premium in crude.

insights.claim: A US-Iran deal brokered via Qatar would likely trigger a rapid normalization of Gulf shipping, given the two-day Hormuz reopening timeline under discussion.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Energy traders should position for a fast supply response if a deal is announced.

insights.claim: President Donald Trump said the US will not launch new attacks on Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections but has not ruled out further military action afterward.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Nov. 3 marks a binary event window for renewed strikes and oil volatility.

insights.claim: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump has not decided whether to launch new strikes against Iran but would prefer to resolve the conflict diplomatically.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Official preference for diplomacy modestly lowers but does not remove escalation odds.

insights.claim: Iran has repeatedly said it would respond to any new attacks by striking US and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Renewed conflict would threaten Gulf host-country assets and infrastructure, widening regional risk.

insights.claim: Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei ordered Iran's armed forces to be prepared for any attack, and the military announced steps to strengthen readiness.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Dual-track posture means talks failure could quickly translate to kinetic escalation.

insights.claim: Iranian negotiators were in Doha for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators, coordinated in regular contacts with Washington.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Qatar is the primary channel to watch for a ceasefire signal.

insights.claim: Araqchi described the talks as ongoing and progressing, with discussions on a two-day proposal continuing but no final conclusion reached, and said Tehran is prepared for both defence and diplomacy.
insights.speaker: Abbas Araqchi
insights.so_what: Progress without closure keeps headline risk two-sided into the midterms.
insights.locator: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said

insights.claim: Araqchi said Iran hopes the other side shows rationality and prioritises diplomacy over other paths.
insights.speaker: Abbas Araqchi
insights.so_what: Iranian rhetoric places the onus on Washington, signaling willingness to deal.
insights.quote: We are doing our best in this process, and we hope that there is rationality on the other side so that they prioritise diplomacy over other paths,
